The pentagon can be placed in the plane with  

\[
A=(0,0),\qquad E=(20,0).
\]

Since \(\angle A=90^\circ\) and \(B\) lies on the same side of \(AE\) as \(C\) and \(D\),  
\(AB\) is vertical; write \(B=(0,b)\) where \(b=AB>0\).

---

### Locating \(C\)

\(\angle B=45^\circ\) means the segment \(BC\) makes a \(45^\circ\) angle with the downward
vertical \(BA\).  Because \(C\) must be to the right of \(AB\) (otherwise \(CD\) would
cross \(AB\)),  

\[
\overrightarrow{BC}=(14,-14),
\qquad\text{so}\qquad 
C=(14,\;b-14).
\]

Thus \(BC=14\sqrt2\) is satisfied automatically.

---

### Locating \(D\)

\(\angle E=90^\circ\) forces \(DE\) to be vertical, so \(D=(20,d)\) with \(d=DE>0\).
At \(D\) the interior angle is \(45^\circ\); the side \(DE\) points down, so \(DC\)
must make a \(45^\circ\) angle with the downward vertical.  

With \(C=(14,b-14)\) and \(D=(20,d)\),

\[
\overrightarrow{DC}=(-6,\;b-14-d).
\]

The angle between \(\overrightarrow{DC}\) and the downward vertical \((0,-1)\) is
\(45^\circ\); hence

\[
\frac{-(b-14-d)}{\sqrt{36+(b-14-d)^2}}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}
\Longrightarrow (b-14-d)^2=36,\; b-14-d<0.
\]

Thus \(b-14-d=-6\), giving  

\[
d=b-8\qquad\text{and}\qquad DE=b-8.
\]

(The condition \(DE<AB\) is automatically satisfied.)

---

### Area of the pentagon

Using the shoelace formula for \(A(0,0),B(0,b),C(14,b-14),D(20,b-8),E(20,0)\):

\[
\text{Area}= \frac12\Bigl|\,\sum x_i y_{i+1}-\sum y_i x_{i+1}\Bigr|
        =20b-164.
\]

(Equivalently, area = area of trapezoid \(ABDE\) minus the fixed triangle \(BCD\)
of area \(84\).)

---

The area must be a multiple of \(16\):

\[
20b-164\equiv0\pmod{16}\Longrightarrow 4b-4\equiv0\pmod{16}
\Longrightarrow b\equiv1\pmod4.
\]

\[
17,\,21,\,25,\dots ,2025.
\]

Number of terms:

\[
\frac{2025-17}{4}+1=\frac{2008}{4}+1=502+1=503.
\]

Thus there are \(\boxed{503}\) possible values of \(AB\).
